NONE: A1 to (cause someone to) become awake and conscious after sleeping
醒來；叫醒，吵醒

C: › the waves that a moving ship or object leaves behind
（航行的船隻等留下的）尾流，航跡

› an occasion when the family and friends of a dead person meet in order to look at the dead body the night before it is buried, or when they meet after a dead person has been buried to drink and talk about the person's life

example: Did you wake at all during the night?
夜裡你一點都沒醒嗎？
Please wake me early tomorrow.
明天請早點叫醒我。
I woke up with a headache.
我醒來時覺得頭痛。
Jane's hand on my shoulder woke me out of/from a bad dream.
簡的手放在我肩上，把我從噩夢中搖醒。
The wake spread out in a v-shape behind the ship.
輪船的航跡呈V字形在船後擴散開來。

NONE: A1 to (cause to) become conscious after sleeping
（某人）醒來；叫醒（某人），弄醒（某人）
› to start to react to a situation after a period in which you have done very little, or to make someone start to react to a situation
（使）（某人）清醒過來，（使）（某人）反應過來

example: Come on, wake up - breakfast is ready.
快點，快醒醒——早飯都準備好了。
He woke himself up with his own snoring!
他打鼾都把自己打醒了！
Companies need to wake up and pay attention to the public's increasing concern about the environment.
各企業需要清醒過來，注意了解公眾對環境的日益關注。

NONE: › used to tell someone that they are wrong about a particular situation and must realize what is really happening
（用於告訴某人）認清形勢，正視目前的情況
› to start to understand that a situation or problem exists
開始意識到（問題）

example: Governments are finally waking up to the fact that the environment should be cleaned up.
各國政府終於開始意識到應該整治環境這個事實。

NONE: › something you say to tell someone to listen or to become involved when they have not been listening or paying attention
注意聽！注意點！

example: Wake up, Daniel! It's your turn.
注意點，丹尼爾！輪到你了。

NONE: › If something that happens is a wake-up call, it should make you realize that you need to take action to change a situation.
警示，警鐘
› a phone call that you arrange to be made, for example in a hotel, to wake you up at a certain time
（旅館、飯店的）電話叫醒服務

example: For the insurance industry, these floods were a wake-up call.
對保險業來說，這些洪水敲響了警鐘。

NONE: › not able to sleep, or used to describe a period of time when you are not able to sleep
不能入睡的；（一段時間內）難以入睡的

example: We spent a wakeful night worrying about where he was.
我們渡過了一個不眠之夜，一直在擔心他去哪裡了。
She lay there wakeful the whole night.
她躺在那裡，徹夜未眠。

NONE: › to (cause to) wake from sleep
醒來；叫醒

example: I shook him but he didn't waken.
我推了推他，但他沒有醒。
Waken me at 7.00, would you?
七點叫醒我，好嗎？

NONE: › said to someone in order to wake them up from sleep
醒醒，醒醒
› the moment when you wake
清醒
› used to refer to a period of time or an experience during which you are awake
清醒的；醒著的

example: For a moment, between waking and sleeping, he couldn't understand where he was.
在半睡半醒之間，他一時不清楚自己身處何處。
She seems to spend every waking moment/minute/hour (= all her available time) at the piano.
她似乎把除睡覺以外的所有時間都花在鋼琴上了。
